title: LLM-XTM: Enhancing Cross-Lingual Topic Models with Large Language Models
subcategory: black-box LLM refinement of cross-lingual topic models
task: Improving coherence and alignment of cross-lingual topics
problem: Cross-lingual topic models depend on sparse bilingual resources; earlier LLM refinements are costly, document-level, hallucination-prone and need white-box token probabilities.
architecture: Post-hoc enhancement of a trained CLTM backbone (InfoCTM, NMTM or XTRA): every f epochs an LLM (e.g. Gemini via API) refines each topic's bilingual top-word pool, filtered by self-consistency uncertainty quantification; an MMD loss keeps original topic-word distributions close to the refined ones; a QA-style document alignment loss matches document-topic distributions to LLM-induced semantic targets.
key_results: With XTRA as backbone: CNPMI +12.8% and TQ +10.5% on EC News; +35.8% coherence and +32.7% TQ on Amazon Review; TU drops by about 2%.
With InfoCTM as backbone, CNPMI rises 51.2% on EC News; on Rakuten Amazon NMTM + LLM-XTM reaches CNPMI 0.016 and TU 0.666 vs 0.012 and 0.633.
strengths: Works with black-box LLM APIs and any VAE-based cross-lingual backbone.
Periodic refinement controls the number of LLM calls.

limitations.text: Cannot rescue a failed backbone: quality is bounded by the initial topics.
Multiple external API calls add latency, unsuitable for real-time or constrained settings.

notes: Small reductions in topic uniqueness are explained by shared core words.
